findings.text: Maps file interface exposes open read seek release and ioctl operations bound to pid maps open seq read seq seek release and procmap ioctl handlers, providing both sequential text iteration and query ioctl on one open file description.

Opening a maps view allocates seq private state sized for proc maps private data, resolves the target address space with read permission, retains it for the lifetime of the description, and releases the private state with address space drop on failure or release.
The maps ioctl entry accepts only the procmap query command and forwards its user argument with the address space captured at open time, rejecting other commands as unsupported.

Sequential maps iteration forms a start next stop cycle where start presenting end sentinel yields termination, gate sentinel yields gate mapping, otherwise first mapping at or after requested offset; next advances until gate then end; stop always balances policy lock address and task holdings.

Two locking configurations exist for maps traversal. One always holds read protection on the address space across the whole range. The other prefers lightweight per mapping protection under read side critical section and transitions irreversibly to address space read protection when per mapping acquisition reports contention, reinitializing iteration at the requested offset.

Procmap address lookup pairs setup with teardown. One configuration never fails setup and teardown releases whichever protection is active. The other acquires killable read protection at setup and releases it at teardown. Lookup under lightweight protection tolerates reference overflow by upgrading to address space protection.

Iteration start retains task and address space references and holds mempolicy and range protection only after both references succeed; stop releases policy protection address reference and task reference and clears the cached task, with no release when no task was retained.

Reported file position always moves forward across merges by recording the end of the last reported mapping and restoring that saved position when iteration resumes from a positive offset, falling back to a gate mapping at end of range rather than stalling at the same start.

Mapping display name follows a fixed priority: file backed mappings show user path unless an anonymous name overrides with shared memory style, then driver supplied name, then architecture name, then vdso for mappings without address space, then heap stack and anonymous named markers.

Each maps line header encodes start and end addresses, four access characters derived from readability writability executability and shareability, file offset, device major minor numbers and inode, followed by optional padded pathname or formatted marker.
File backed mappings report device inode and offset from the user visible inode, dereferencing backing file identity when the file operates as an overlay, otherwise using the direct file inode.

Address query selects the first mapping satisfying optional file backed requirement and optional permission subset, returning a covering mapping or optionally the next satisfying mapping, otherwise signaling absence; iteration advances by mapping end when skipping.

Procmap query validates user sizing before access, rejecting oversize descriptors, undersize descriptors lacking address fields, unknown flag bits, and unpaired name or build identifier address length pairs.

Successful query returns mapping bounds, translated permission bits, kernel page size, file offset device and inode with zeros for anonymous mappings, plus optional variable length name and build identifier truncated by path limit and reported with required sizes, with all user copies performed after releasing locks and address reference.

Memory size accounting uses a counters structure holding plain byte totals for residency sharing dirtiness access anonymity and special mappings plus fixed point proportional share totals with separate breakdowns for origin dirtiness and lock state.

Proportional share accounting attributes each charged portion to exactly one of anonymous shared memory or file buckets, additionally to locked and dirty buckets when applicable, and to shared versus private clean dirty counters according to dirtiness and exclusivity.

Page table entry scanning distinguishes present mappings, empty slots delegated to hole handling, swap entries charged to swap totals with share divided by swap count, and device private or framed entries treated as present for accounting, ignoring entries without an associated page.

Transparent huge page scanning ignores empty entries, treats present entries as present and migration capable nonpresent framed entries as nonpresent, classifies large folios into anonymous shared memory or file huge totals while ignoring device zoned folios, then applies compound accounting with young dirty and lock state; an alternate configuration provides an empty handler performing no accounting.
Proportional share values use fixed point scaling with shift twelve.
Queryable mapping permission mask combines readable writable executable and shared bits; valid query mask further allows covering or next and file backed selectors.

Transient contention during mapping acquisition retries after upgrading protection while other mapping errors propagate; interruptible lock failure, missing task or address space, oversize or malformed query, allocation failure, overlong names, user copy faults and unsupported ioctl each map to distinct negative errors with cleanup of held references buffers and files.
Hole accounting charges partial shared memory swap usage over the hole range when shared memory support provides a hole callback, otherwise hole handling is absent and contributes nothing.
